evidence: The bug concerns CSS overscroll-behavior scroll propagation behavior, which is a layout/scroll rendering concern owned by the Layout team.
Platform Win32 handle bug (CloseHandle on RegisterWaitForSingleObject wait handle) in KeyWatcher maps to Core::Widget: Win32 under OS Integration.
Bug describes a computed panel UI issue with OutputParser and shape-outside value, consistent with DevTools Inspector.
The use-after-free is in nsAnimationManager::DoUpdateAnimations in layout/style, owned by the Layout team.
Split views inside collapsed tab groups disappearing after session restore points to tab/group frontend features like Firefox::Tabbed Browser: Split View and Tab Groups.
The bug is about the address bar trust panel (unified trust panel icon) on neterror and about: pages, which belongs to the address bar UI team.
The bug involves the urlbar (address bar) and its taskbartab check, which is owned by Search Next Generation.
crashreporter client build id derivation failure points to crash reporting/build tooling owned by CI and Quality Tools.
The bug is about the URL bar input box margin in RTL, and Firefox::Address Bar (under Search Next Generation) owns the URL bar UI.
Bug involves pointer lock mouse event handling in EventStateManager and synthesized event dispatch, matching DOM: UI Events & Focus Handling in DOM Core.
All prior similar bugs about search engine name/URL updates, Glean search telemetry, and search engine icons/default handling were routed to Search Next Generation.
Build failure on OpenBSD due to missing libdl, a platform-specific shared library dependency, which is typically handled by OS Integration.
The crash and UAF are in dom/indexedDB/ActorsParent.cpp with PBackgroundIDBRequest IPC, matching the many already-routed indexedDB bugs assigned to DOM LWS.
The bug describes Android bundled fonts in omni.ja not loading, referencing font-list code and nsZipCursor, which points to the Layout font-handling team.

The ClearOnShutdown assertion fires from CookieService::Init during the backup scheduler test, but similar prior reports with ClearOnShutdown were routed to Telemetry, so I lean that way with lower confidence while Networking (CookieService) and Privacy Engineering (cookies) are alternatives.
The crash stack in ToJSValue.cpp/ScriptSettings.cpp involves DOM bindings and script settings, pointing to DOM-related teams.
The report concerns the about:preferences Applications settings UI rows for file types, matching the series of already-routed Frontend bugs about that same settings list.
The bug mentions Widevine/GMP playback on Netflix and Amazon, which is typically owned by the Media team.
The Trust panel/site identity panel is owned by Privacy Engineering's Firefox::Site Identity component.
The bug reports have hints of timing out, but without a clear component or module reference, the most likely teams based on similar past bugs are Layout, GFX, and DevTools.
Heap use-after-free in nsPipe::mInputList — nsPipe is the Necko/networking pipe implementation in netwerk/base.
Crash occurs in layout engine code (nsBlockFrame, nsFlexContainerFrame) with fragmentation assertions, matching prior bugs routed to Layout.

The InvalidStateError arises in the urlbar actor message path (UrlbarParentController/UrlbarChildControllerProxy in browser/components/urlbar), which belongs to the Firefox::Address Bar component owned by Search Next Generation.
window.open popup behavior and chrome flags are handled by nsWindowWatcher under OS Integration (window management).
The 'Learn more' link in the neterror page template is misdirected, and error page templates are owned by Toolkit::Error Pages which maps to Frontend.

The bug concerns duplicate borders between the notificationbox and the RDM toolbar in split view, referencing DevTools-specific CSS (splitters/RDM toolbar) and an existing DevTools CSS rule to remove.
The bug concerns the built-in password manager being disabled by an extension and the reset button in Privacy & Security settings, which maps to Credential Management.
All prior DAMP devtools performance regressions were routed to DevTools.
test_takeFocus.xhtml and FocusManager/DOMMenuItemActive suggest focus handling, owned by DOM Core's UI Events & Focus Handling, though the tree row activation could also be Accessibility.
Bug mentions SearchWidgetTracker and CustomizableUI widget placement/visibility, matching the Firefox::Search component owned by Search Next Generation.

The bug concerns a clipped illustration/SVG asset on net and certificate error pages (about:neterror illustrations), and prior similar 'Icon is clipped on SSL Network-Error pages' and 'Restart Required header/text smaller' error-page bugs were routed to the team owning net-error page visuals, matchi
SERP categorization hash update for non-ASCII domains relates to search telemetry, owned by Search Next Generation (Firefox::Search).

After opening a PDF, Firefox requests favicon.ico without session context; this likely relates to how the PDF viewer (pdf.js) loads or creates the document, but favicon fetching is a networking/DOM-level behavior.
Report concerns unsafe IPC ParamTraits/serialization deserialization of widget events (IPC, type confusion), matching Core::IPC owned by OS Integration.
Bug concerns SourceSurfaceWebgl/DrawTargetWebgl shared surface expiration and unmap race, mapping directly to the Core::Graphics: CanvasWebGL/WebRender components owned by GFX.
The leak involves IPC actor lifetime and document persistence tied to browser frontend saving behavior, pointing to Frontend ownership of the save flow.

The title '[CTW] Bounds incorrect for text within translated, absolute positioned Accessibles within section acc' and problem description about accessible element bounds point to Accessibility (CTW refers to caching the world for accessible bounds).
Build-system bustage (mozbuild/Python configure errors) maps to OS Integration, which owns the platform build/tooling components.
The bug is an assertion failure in SpiderMonkey's ICU4X collator, reached via Intl.Collator.prototype.compare, which is owned by the Javascript team.
Tab note UI and theme colors are handled by the Firefox frontend team.

The bug concerns the tracking protection panel's toggle HCM styling, which is owned by the Privacy: Anti-Tracking component under Privacy Engineering (mirroring the similar shield-icon tracking panel routing).
The bug involves a VPN status toggle widget rendering with wrong size inside the overflow menu after being moved there, which is overflow-menu/toolbar customization widget layout owned by Frontend.
The report references incomplete work from m-c (Bug 2046258) requiring an additional fix in m-c for Thunderbird, likely a frontend layout/interaction fix.
All frames and file paths reference js/src/wasm, the JavaScript engine's WebAssembly implementation.
Crash stack and style/servo rule cache poisoning code all live in layout/style, owned by Layout team.
New wpt failures in /svg/animations/ about SVG animateMotion path animation, closest to Layout's SVG component.
The bug is a UI style refinement for the Nova Spotlight template, a user-facing messaging/onboarding surface whose template styling and CTA button rendering is owned by Frontend.
The bug mentions DecodePropertyIPDL, an IPC serialization mechanism likely owned by DOM content-process code (DOM LWS).
Crash in Android system font API initialization (gfxAndroidPlatform::IsFontAPIDisabled / AndroidSystemFontIterator) belongs to the GFX-owned Core::Graphics: Text fonts code.
Private Browsing mode-specific page loading failures match prior Privacy Engineering bugs.
The bug is about XULButtonAccessible in accessible/xul/XULFormControlAccessible.cpp, an accessibility component.
The bug concerns the styling (missing borders) of buttons inside the CC/Address/Password save doorhangers, which are part of the form autofill feature owned by Credential Management.
Scrolling and paint-skip (tp5o_scroll, tscrollx) regressions on WebRender typically trace to the graphics/compositor layer.
Report concerns Metal ANGLE/WebGL shader compilation and DrawTargetWebgl shaders, owned by the GFX component.
The report mentions 'media-triage-bot', pointing to the Media team's triage bot.
Build error in js/src/jit/*/Simulator-*.cpp about JS JIT simulator prototypes, matching prior bugs routed to Javascript.
The bug references netwerk/protocol/http, nsSocketTransport, and speculative connections, matching the Networking team's ownership of Core::Networking components.
JPEG XL image decoding performance maps to the image decoding component Core::Graphics: ImageLib owned by GFX.
The bug concerns lifetime management of Media IPDL actors (RemoteMediaDataEncoderChild/RemoteCDMChild), matching the Media component that owns Audio/Video GMP and encoder IPDL code.
The test name suggests an intermittent failure in a WebRTC mDNS candidate obfuscation test, which falls under WebRTC and networking, typically handled by the Media team.
Crash in ANGLE's CopyBGRA8ToRGBA8Fast via WebGL readPixels, code under gfx/angle, owned by GFX.
The assertion is triggered by FOG::InitializeFOG, which is part of Glean/Telemetry shutdown handling.
Bug is in widget/gtk/nsGtkKeyUtils.cpp, GTK platform widget code, which is owned by OS Integration (Core::Widget: Gtk).
The bug concerns window.open creating a chrome:// tab and resizing the parent window, which relates to top-level window and tab management handled by the Frontend team.
Crash stack shows layout frame style reparenting in nsIFrame and RestyleManager, typical of Layout component failures.
Crash is in nsTextFrame::GetSelectionDetails called from nsDisplayText rendering in layout/generic, pointing to the text frame/layout code owner.
Service worker fetch interception failures are owned by DOM LWS's Service Workers component, with Networking and DevTools as secondary candidates.
Networking issue likely related to HTTP/2 CONNECT or proxy handling, since the connection gets stuck after redirect.

The File > Work Offline menu item lives in Firefox's menu bar (Firefox::Menus), which sits under the Frontend/Search Next Generation application-features group, and the checkbox state sync issue points to browser UI rather than the networking backend.
The report is about UI design inconsistencies vs a Figma spec, similar to previously routed Frontend visual-mismatch bugs (tab pickup font sizes, Firefox View states).
Custom cursor implementation lives in platform widget code (widget/cocoa/MOZDynamicCursor.mm), owned by OS Integration's Core::Widget platform components.

The bug centers on backdrop-filter being disabled/blocklisted on some graphics drivers, causing PDF text selection to be invisible, pointing to the graphics/backdrop-filter implementation owned by GFX.

The bug is a UI widget (ConfirmationHint popup) regression in browser base content relying on popup open/timer and panel CSS, matching Frontend/confirmation-hint ownership rather than backend places or search components.
The bug concerns VPN CFR/onboarding message behavior driven by Nimbus experiments, matching the messaging system owned by Onboarding, Messaging, and Communication.
Crash assertion is in gfx/wr/webrender source, matching prior fuzzing crashes routed to GFX.
CSP reporting implementation leaking cross-origin URL information is a content security feature owned by Security Engineering (Core::DOM: Security).
Heap use-after-free in dom/file/MutableBlobStorage.cpp involving PTemporaryIPCBlobChild, an IPDL PBackground actor under Core::DOM: File (DOM LWS).
The bug concerns unlabeled toggles in the about:preferences Search reorderable list, which are owned by the search settings UI (Search Next Generation) with accessibility labeling concerns.
The bug is a CSS Typed OM test failure about animation-duration computed value, which relates to CSS property implementation handled by the Layout team.
The warning comes from widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp, a graphics/WebGL DMABuf fence issue tied to GFX's rendering stack.
The bug is about CSS border-radius, overflow:hidden, and filter clipping, which is a rendering/layout issue involving border-radius geometry, most likely in Layout although it could overlap GFX.
Browser chrome test (browser_mozicon_file.js) disabled by an erroneous skip-if involving a browser pref (nova), matching prior browser UI test-disabling bugs routed to Frontend.
Backtrace shows crash in js::wasm::TypeContext and JavaScript engine wasm code.
GlyphCacheEntry is a font glyph caching structure that belongs to the graphics subsystem, making GFX the owning team.
Crash stack frames are all in gfx/harfbuzz (font shaping), which belongs to the GFX team.

The bug reports an incorrect messaging_system.message_id in impression telemetry for a Spotlight message, which matches the MESSAGING/onboarding experiment pattern seen in prior correctly-routed bugs to Onboarding, Messaging, and Communication.
Print output showing wrong colors (color instead of black-and-white) is a rendering/printing output issue owned by Layout, which handles Printing: Output.
The bug concerns the searchbar and ContextualSearch/TabToSearch, matching the Firefox::Search component owned by Search Next Generation.
Infinite-loop in querySelector points to DOM selector matching, typically owned by DOM Core.
The report describes HTTP/2 RST_STREAM handling in Http2Session.cpp resulting in NS_ERROR_NET_RESET, which is Necko networking code.
Crash in nsJARChannel::GetContentTypeGuess and nsJARProtocolHandler::MimeService indicates networking file/jar protocol handling, pointing to Networking.
The bug involves privacy browsing mode and clearing site data, directly matching the Privacy Engineering team's known routing pattern for similar issues.
Profile selector dialog and profile launching behavior point to Frontend (Firefox::General/Profile management UI), as seen in similar already-routed bugs.
Crash originates in parakeet.cpp speech-recognition inference called from dom/media/webspeech/recognition/SpeechRecognitionParent.cpp, so the owning media/web-speech team is the likely fix owner.
Screen reader fails to read confirmation dialog text in the 'End Private Session' flow, matching the known Private Browsing dialog accessibility bug owned by Privacy Engineering.
Bug concerns Firefox View/split view tab and tab group behavior, matching the Frontend components (Firefox::Firefox View, Firefox::Tabbed Browser: Split View/Tab Groups).
Crash stack traces reference dom/media/webrtc files (RTCDTMFSender, RTCRtpTransceiver, MediaPipeline), which are owned by the Media team.
The failure is in a WebAssembly off-thread compile test, pointing to the JavaScript engine's WebAssembly implementation.
Bug involves History/Places storage of page titles and POST visit skipping, which is owned by Places (Toolkit::Places) under Search Next Generation.
